sections.h2: Allen County tax offices and what each one does
sections.html:
Property tax in Allen County runs through two desks in Scottsville. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) decides what each parcel is worth. The Sheriff takes the payment. Nothing the PVA does sets the tax rate. Your bill comes from that assessed value times levies from the county, the school board and taxing districts like the library and the health department.

Where to call in Scottsville
OfficeAddressPhone
Property Valuation Administrator201 W Main St #1, Scottsville, KY 42164(270) 237-3711
Sheriff, tax collector194 W Wood St, Scottsville, KY 42164(270) 237-3210
Sheriff, owners who never received a billScottsville(270) 237-3388

The PVA keeps weekday hours until 4:30 p.m. Online, the sheriff's page offers a tax bill search by owner or parcel, and the PVA's page carries the certified roll with ownership details.

Kentucky freezes both value and ownership on January 1. Buy in June and the bill for that year is still addressed to whoever owned on January 1. The PVA tries to send the new owner a copy using the deed on record. If no copy shows up, phone the sheriff instead of waiting.

Four price points govern an Allen County bill under KRS 134.015: a 2 percent reduction for paying in full through November 1, the face amount during the rest of the year's last two months, a 5 percent surcharge in January, and a 10 percent surcharge from February onward.

The sheriff's work ends on April 15. At close of business, whatever is still unpaid transfers to the clerk, and each account becomes a recorded lien called a certificate of delinquency. Any sale has to wait at least 90 days and must happen within 135. Notices come from the county attorney during that stretch, and the clerk publishes the delinquent list a month or longer beforehand.

After the handoff the balance climbs by 1 percent each month, and the clerk and county attorney collect commissions. Kentucky's sample account begins with a $1,000 bill. Paid within five business days of the transfer it costs $1,387.79. After the county attorney's first notice it is $1,611.30, and it reaches $1,704.21 if an investor pays it at the tax sale. The sample uses assumed rates, so your own payoff will vary somewhat.

You can't skip the PVA. A sit-down with the PVA or a deputy has to happen before an appeal is taken, and the roll can be inspected for 13 days counting from the first Monday of May. The PVA publishes those dates in the newspaper with the widest circulation.

When the meeting is over, take the appeal to the county clerk by the next workday after inspection closes. Local property owners sit as the review board, and they meet between 25 and 35 days after inspection ends. Bring photos showing condition, repair bids, insurance paperwork and recent nearby sales. The board looks only at evidence presented while you and the PVA's representative are both present, and a changed value must be explained in writing.

You're free to make an audio recording of the hearing. Bills printed before a decision use the figure from your form, and a higher final value brings a second bill for the difference, which is why a realistic number matters.

sections.h2: The state rate and a typical Allen County home
sections.html:
The statewide real property rate for 2025 is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value. It was 10.9 cents in 2024. Levies from the county and local districts go on top, and the sheriff's bill search lists the complete amount for a given parcel. The midpoint value for an owner-occupied home is $192,300, a fair marker for where most Allen County owners sit.

The early-payment discount of 2 percent reduces the entire bill, local levies included.

Kentucky lets homeowners aged 65 or over, and those classed as totally disabled, shave $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026. The reduction happens before any tax rate is applied.

Reaching 65 doesn't switch it on. The application goes to the Allen County PVA at (270) 237-3711. A claim based on disability must be renewed each year, with two exceptions: owners whose disability came from military service, and owners ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: Checking your own account before you sell
sections.html:
Before listing the house, spend ten minutes confirming three things. First, search the sheriff's page for your parcel and see whether the current bill shows as paid. Second, look at the PVA's roll to make sure the owner names and the description match your deed. Third, if you've held the house since before 2025, ask the PVA whether a homestead claim is on file and whether it needs renewing.

An error caught early costs one phone call. Mistakes found by a title examiner a week before closing cost time, and sometimes a buyer's patience. A mismatch in a name, such as a late spouse still listed, is the usual culprit, and the PVA is the office that corrects it.

A tax lien attaches to the land, not to you personally. The statute lets it live until someone pays it or eleven years go by, and a sale doesn't end it. Expect the buyer's title company to find it and insist on a payoff, either before closing or out of what you'd receive.

  1. Ask the Allen County Sheriff to write down the balance shortly before the closing date.
  2. When the account has already moved to the clerk, the clerk gives that number instead, with interest and commissions included.
  3. Your closing agent subtracts the payoff from your share and files the release.
  4. Put the buyer's mailing address in the file so next year's bill finds them.

Selling for cash removes lender appraisals and repair demands. It does not remove the lien, which gets paid at the closing table in the same way.

The county borders Tennessee. Scottsville is the seat and the only city. The 2020 census counted 20,588 people, and the July 2025 federal estimate is 22,536, up 9.5 percent. Housing units numbered 9,390 in 2025, and 74.5 percent of occupied homes are owned. Just 17 building permits were issued in 2025, which means buyers mostly choose among existing houses. US 231 is a four-lane parkway connecting Scottsville to Interstate 65, roughly 30 miles off.

Some county records burned in a 1902 courthouse fire, which can slow a title search on a very old parcel. For most sellers the smoothest closings come from a recorded deed that reads cleanly and a tax account showing nothing owed.

faqs.q: Which Allen County office takes tax payments?
faqs.a: The sheriff takes them, as KRS 134.140 and 160.500 provide. Go to 194 W Wood St in Scottsville or call (270) 237-3210. The PVA only values property.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Allen County taxes late?
faqs.a: January adds 5 percent and later months add 10 percent. After April 15 the clerk takes over the account, and interest of 1 percent monthly plus extra fees start accruing.

faqs.q: Is the Allen County homestead exemption automatic at age 65?
faqs.a: No. You must apply at the Allen County PVA. For 2025 and 2026 the amount is $49,100, and you need to be 65 or older or totally disabled.

faqs.q: I bought a house in Allen County after January 1. Who gets the tax bill?
faqs.a: The previous owner. Kentucky locks in ownership on January 1, so the bill carries that name. The PVA attempts to mail you a duplicate from the deed, and the sheriff can help if none arrives.

faqs.q: Can an Allen County tax lien block a sale?
faqs.a: Yes, it can stall a closing. KRS 134.420 keeps the lien on the parcel until payment or eleven years, and a buyer would inherit it. Get the sheriff's payoff figure and settle it at the table.
